idiom_name: named value type carrying the recurring parameter group
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: declare a type whose members are exactly the values that keep travelling together, name it after the concept they represent, and let every caller construct one instance instead of listing the values. Keep it immutable (constructed once, no setters) and let it own the group's defaults, validation and group-level queries; the callee then declares a single parameter of that type. Where the language generates value semantics (records, data classes, case classes), the classic class with constructor, accessors and equality is unnecessary; where it does not, write initialization and comparison helpers once beside the type instead of repeating them at call sites.
pitfalls: Grouping unrelated values into one carrier (a junk-drawer object) hides the real coupling and is worse than the parameter list it replaced.
Letting the callee mutate the carrier, or the caller keep it alive afterwards, turns argument passing into hidden shared state.
Introducing a type for a group used by a single call site adds indirection without removing any duplication.
